decisions.justification: The agent asked which freshness policy to use, and the user chose “Ad hoc fresh, nightly cached.”
The selected option specified that normal CLI runs bypass the six-hour cache, which the agent restated as always reflecting the current orders.json.
The options explicitly contrasted preserving cached nightly operation with risking the ten-minute limit, and the user chose nightly caching.
The chosen option explicitly proposed an opt-in cache option for the nightly script, later concretized as --cache and approved by the user.
The agent never asked whether an export must represent one consistent point in time or may mix source versions.
The transcript never settles what an in-progress export should do if orders.json is rewritten during its read.
The selected approach explicitly avoids cache validation on the fresh path by bypassing the cache entirely.
The agent never asked or established what the CLI should emit when valid source data cannot be obtained.
No question or implementation detail addresses retries when a read races the sync job.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The session selected and implemented a clear bounded approach that preserves nightly caching while making ad hoc exports fresh, and it avoided all forbidden questions. However, the questioning was shallow: after one bundled approach question it moved to an approval gate without covering snapshot consistency, concurrent rewrites, failure output, or retry bounds.
